title: 2021 Octaviasta, motonetin hinta, kuluttajariitalautakunta
subtitle: Appendix 4 — proper nouns, brand words, and institutional vocabulary

blocks.text: A few words in this corpus are proper nouns, brand names, or references to Finnish institutions — car models, a hardware chain, a consumer dispute board. These don't need grammar explanations so much as simple context, so you're not left guessing what a capitalised word refers to.

blocks.content: {Octavia|word|proper noun|Škoda Octavia (car model)} and {Focus|word|proper noun|Ford Focus (car model)} are specific car models mentioned by name in reviews — exactly the kind of detail that makes a complaint feel concrete and verifiable. {Motonetti|word|proper noun|a Nordic car-parts retail chain} is a well-known parts retailer, referenced when a reviewer compares a shop's price to the 'normal' retail price.

items.fi: Eilen katsastuksessa 2021 {Octaviasta|grammar|elative of Octavia|from the Octavia} oli yllättäen takapuslat vaihtokunnossa.
items.en: At yesterday's inspection, the 2021 Octavia unexpectedly had rear bushings needing replacement.

items.fi: Hyvin hoiti meidän {Focuksen|grammar|accusative of Focus|the Focus}.
items.en: Took great care of our Focus.

blocks.title: Where Finnish complaints go to escalate
blocks.text: {Kuluttajariitalautakunta|word|compound proper noun|the Finnish Consumer Disputes Board} is a real Finnish government body that mediates disputes between consumers and businesses. It appears repeatedly in the corpus's most serious complaints as the next step after a shop refuses to resolve an issue directly — kuluttajariitalautakunnan päätöksen jälkeen, 'after the Consumer Disputes Board's decision'. You already met {vakuutusyhtiö|word|compound noun|insurance company} in Lesson 25.

items.fi: Eivät ota mitään vastuuta edes {kuluttajariitalautakunnan|grammar|genitive, long compound|the Consumer Disputes Board's} päätöksen saatuaan.
items.en: They take no responsibility even after receiving the Consumer Disputes Board's decision.

items.fi: {Vakuutusyhtiö|word|compound noun|insurance company} totesi, että diagnoosi oli virheellinen.
items.en: The insurance company stated that the diagnosis was incorrect.

blocks.content: {TM-testi|word|proper noun|a comparison test run by Tekniikan Maailma, a Finnish technology/motoring magazine} refers to a well-known consumer-comparison test. Sai pohjat TM-testissä (also seen as an idiom in the previous appendix lesson) specifically means the shop scored lowest in that magazine's published comparison.

items.fi: Ei ihme että tämä korjaamo sai pohjat {TM-testissä|grammar|inessive, proper noun|in the TM test}.
items.en: No wonder this repair shop scored at the bottom in the TM test.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Which car did you take to the repair shop?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: 2021 Octavian. Hinta oli paljon kalliimpi kuin Motonetin hinta samasta osasta.
lines.en: A 2021 Octavia. The price was much higher than Motonetti's price for the same part.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Did you take the matter to the Consumer Disputes Board?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Vein, mutta korjaamo ei noudattanut päätöstä silti.
lines.en: I did, but the repair shop still didn't follow the decision.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: Proper nouns and institutional names are context, not grammar — you don't need to analyse them morphologically, just recognise them for what they refer to. Once you know kuluttajariitalautakunta is a real dispute-resolution body and TM-testi is a magazine comparison, the sentences around them become far less mysterious.

blocks.content: Kuluttajariitalautakunta: a genuinely long compound — break it at ku-lut-ta-ja (consumer) + rii-ta (dispute) + lau-ta-kun-ta (board), and say each piece separately before joining them. Octavia: OK-ta-vi-a (as in English, lightly Finnicized). Motonetti: MO-to-net-ti (double t held).
